subject: Preflight Preparation - Certification Requirements (Sightseeing Exception)
learning_objective: State the authorization requirements for local, non-stop sightseeing flights conducted for compensation.
question_text: As a commercial pilot, you decide to start a small business flying non-stop tours to look at Christmas lights during the holiday season. What authorizations, if any, are required to conduct Christmas light tours?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No authorizations or approvals are required if you hold the appropriate category and class rating for the aircraft that will be flown.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You must apply for and receive a Letter of Authorization from a Flight Standards District Office.

choices.label: C
choices.text: You must apply to the FAA to receive an exemption to carry passengers at night within a 50 mile radius of your departure airport.

explanation: 14 CFR 119.1(e) exempts certain nonstop sightseeing flights conducted within a limited radius of the departure airport from Part 119's air-carrier/operating-certificate requirements, so a commercial pilot with the appropriate category/class rating may conduct such local sightseeing flights under Part 91 without additional Part 119 authorization.

incorrect_answer_explanations.B: No FSDO Letter of Authorization is required for this specific, regulation-defined sightseeing exception.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: No special night-passenger-carrying exemption process applies here; the operation is simply outside Part 119's scope under the sightseeing-flight exception.
